title: Introduce RAG telemetry diff-watcher and structured-assertion harness
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: debugging regressions in RAG authoring is hard because transient streaming differences and structured-output drift (JSON schemas, tool-call arguments) are noisy and unclear in CI. This PR adds a small examples + docs + test harness that (1) captures streaming token and event traces from local runs, (2) computes a compact structured diff between expected and observed tool-calls and JSON outputs, and (3) exposes an assertions DSL to pin prompt-based expectations. The goal is not to be a full test framework but to provide a reproducible, low-friction toolset for developers and authoring workflows.

What this PR contains: lightweight CLI (node) for running a replay-and-diff flow, a Python prober to generate compact reference traces from offline indexes, an examples template that demonstrates asserting structured output from a RAG agent (tool-call arguments, final JSON schema), and a docs site page with authoring guidance and suggested CI patterns. Also includes unit tests and a GitHub Actions workflow for smoke validation.

Key features: compact event trace format (newline-delimited JSON events), configurable canonicalization and lossy-normalization rules (timestamps, streaming chunking, token-level differences), structured-assertion DSL supporting path-matchers, optional fuzzy-string thresholds, and auto-generated failure summaries with a small visual diff. The harness also supports toggling between gold-trace comparison and policy-based assertions (allowing partial matches).

Checklist: 
- [x] Add CLI and example repo scaffolding
- [x] Add docs site page + snippets for authoring guide
- [x] Add smoke CI workflow (actions)
- [x] Add unit tests for diff engine and assertion DSL
- [x] Notify SRE for potential CI costs

Design notes: the diff engine intentionally avoids token-by-token diffs on streaming output; instead it attempts to reconstruct logical outputs (tool_call events, final assistant JSON) by reassembling stream fragments and applying canonicalizers. The assertions DSL is JSON-path based and intentionally conservative: by default it fails loudly on missing keys but permits fuzziness for strings/numbers via explicit flags.

Testing & validation: local smoke runs validated against a recorded reference trace for the "kb-qa" example included. CI runs the smoke workflow which spins a small local stub (node http mock) that returns deterministic tool responses and compares the resulting trace to the committed gold trace.

Rollout plan: merge to main guarded behind small feature flag in examples CI; docsite copy is additive and non-breaking. We'll follow-up with a short internal demo to devtools and authoring teams and create a Linear task to expand gold-trace coverage for selected playbooks.

Related work: complements the existing RAG authoring quickstarts but focuses on deterministic trace diffs and structured assertions instead of live playground UX. See linked Linear tasks.

Notes on compatibility: this is purely examples + dev tooling and does not change runtime code paths. It is safe for mainline and intended for developer productivity only.

release_notes: Adds a developer-oriented RAG trace diff watcher and assertion harness under examples/rag-diff-watcher. Includes CLI, small Python prober, docs page, and CI smoke workflow. Intended for authoring/debug workflows and CI smoke tests.
